notes.meaning: Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Their families became the three main branches of the tribe of Levi, who were set apart to serve God. This opening shows that the temple workers had clear family records reaching back to Israel's earliest ancestors.

Kohath had four sons named Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath is highlighted first because the priests came from his branch of the family. God chose this specific family line to oversee the most sacred parts of Israel's worship.

Amram's children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, three famous leaders of Israel. Aaron served as the first high priest, while his sons Nadab and Abihu died for disobeying God, leaving Eleazar and Ithamar to continue the work. This reminds believers to honor God with deep reverence in holy things.

The line of priests moved from Aaron through Eleazar to his son Phinehas, and then to Abishua. Phinehas was well known for his fierce loyalty to God during Israel's travels in the desert. God honored that faithful devotion by preserving his family as high priests.

This list traces the priestly line through Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah, Meraioth, Amariah, and Ahitub. Around the time of Uzzi, the high priest's duties shifted for a while to Ithamar's family before later returning to this line. Even when history records little about these men, God quietly kept His promises to their family.

Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz. Zadok served faithfully during King David's reign, bringing the office of high priest back into Eleazar's family line just as God had promised. Loyal service to the Lord outlasts the rise and fall of earthly kings.

Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah, whose son was Johanan, the father of another Azariah. This Azariah served faithfully in the great temple that King Solomon built in Jerusalem, likely standing firm against King Uzziah when the king tried to take over priestly duties. God remembers and honors leaders who stand up bravely for true worship.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars believe the note about serving in Solomon's temple originally belonged to the first Azariah in verse 9, having shifted down through a copying error.

notes.meaning: Azariah was the father of Amariah, and Amariah was the father of Ahitub. This Amariah was the high priest who led the nation in spiritual matters during the reign of King Jehoshaphat. God faithfully provided wise spiritual helpers to guide His people through changing times.

Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Shallum. These men continued the steady work of the priesthood during the later years of Judah's monarchy. God preserved the holy service in His house through generations of steady, quiet devotion.

Shallum was the father of Hilkiah, and Hilkiah was the father of Azariah. Hilkiah is famous for discovering the forgotten Book of the Law in the temple, which sparked King Josiah's great religious renewal. God's word has the power to bring new life to people even after years of neglect.

Azariah was the father of Seraiah, and Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak. Seraiah was the high priest when Babylon captured Jerusalem, and he was put to death by the invaders. Even in that dark defeat, God spared his son so the priestly line would not end.

Jehozadak was carried off into captivity when the Lord sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile through King Nebuchadnezzar. The writer emphasizes that God Himself was directing events, correcting His people when they turned away from Him. Even during painful seasons of discipline, God never forgets His covenant people.

The record names Levi's three sons again as Gershom, Kohath, and Merari, and lists Gershom's sons as Libni and Shimei. The focus here turns away from the high priests to the other Levite families who served in temple music and daily care. Every kind of service in God's work holds an honored place.

Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, while Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These men led the major clans within the tribe of Levi. Each family had its own special duties in caring for the house of the Lord.

This list follows the family line of Gershom through seven generations down to Jeatherai. These descendants served the sanctuary over many years leading up to the reign of King David. God values the long-term dedication of families who remain faithful across generations.

These verses trace the line of Kohath through Amminadab and Korah down to Shaul. Although Korah famously rebelled in the desert, God spared his children, and their descendants became praised worship leaders in Israel. God's mercy can turn a difficult family past into a legacy of praise.

This family record traces the line of Elkanah down through several generations to another Elkanah, the father of the prophet Samuel. By recording these names, the writer confirms that Samuel had true Levite heritage before he began serving God at the tabernacle. God carefully prepares the family background of His servants before calling them to their work.
